co_primary_metric_rationale: Each derivative coordinate is fixed before sampling and occupies the same relative first-layer Bloch-Messiah block across N and L.
co_primary_metrics: Var_theta[dC/dtheta_i] for the matched passive coordinate
Var_theta[dC/dtheta_i] for the matched squeezing coordinate
Var_theta[dC/dtheta_i] for the matched displacement coordinate
cost_specificity: Every conclusion is specific to the fixed scalar homodyne MSE cost and the recorded initialization ensemble.

execution.failure_policy: A failed, timed-out, or OOM-killed architecture is recorded and does not prevent later architectures from running.

finite_size_interpretation: This diagnostic probes only the accessible N<=5 and L<=3 regime. It neither establishes nor excludes an asymptotic barren plateau.

inactive_coordinate_definition.interpretation: Numerical diagnostic only; it is reported because pooling a size-dependent number of inactive coordinates can bias global median summaries.

initialization.legacy_uniform: Independent U[0,1) parameters, matching the historical initialization distribution, not a selected old vector.

literature_context.reference: B. Zhang and Q. Zhuang, Energy-dependent barren plateau in bosonic variational quantum circuits, arXiv:2305.01799; Quantum Sci. Technol. 10, 015009 (2025).
literature_context.scope_caveat: That result treats different bosonic variational ansatze and costs. It is context, not a theorem asserted for this conditionally normalized Gaussian-plus-ladder QONN.

paired_design: K and energy scale are excluded from the parameter seed, so fixed-N,L comparisons reuse the underlying random draws.
secondary_metrics: mean squared gradient per parameter and total gradient norm
Gaussian-core photons per mode and in total
width_resource_caveat: The scalar input carries fixed total displacement energy, not fixed energy per mode, while initialized trainable operations can add size-dependent energy. Measured total and per-mode core energies are therefore reported, and the width scan is not a direct test of a fixed-per-mode-energy theorem.
